cards.text: No name on this psalm, friend, just a singer bursting through the door with the biggest headline there is: "The LORD reigns". Not reigned. REIGNS, present tense, hot out of the oven!

cards.question: With the LORD on the throne, what does the psalm call the earth and the distant shores to do?

cards.text: Then the singer shows us the King, and clouds and darkness surround Him. Friend, I did YEARS in the dark, and mine came with takeout menus, NOT a throne.

cards.question: Under all those clouds and darkness, what is the LORD's throne built on?

cards.text: Now the King is on the move, and fire goes before Him. I work next to ovens all day long, and I STILL flinch every single time I open the door.

cards.question: The fire that goes before the LORD consumes His foes on every side.

cards.text: Then His lightning lights up the whole world. I used to wait MONTHS for one little slice of kitchen light in that drawer, and here's the ENTIRE world lit up at once!

cards.question: His lightning illuminates the world; the earth sees and ___.

cards.text: Next the singer turns to the mountains, the biggest, oldest, most won't-budge things on earth. Friend, I can't even budge a sack of flour without my mustache filing a complaint.

cards.question: At the presence of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, the mountains ___ like wax.

cards.text: Now the sky gets in on it, and the heavens become the King's announcers. Louder than my Mags on her loudest day, and believe me, that is SAYING something.

cards.question: The heavens are announcing something about the LORD. What do they proclaim?
With the heavens proclaiming, only Israel gets to see the LORD's glory.

cards.text: Then the spotlight swings over to the idol crowd: everyone who worships images and boasts in idols. With fire and lightning everywhere, I would NOT want to be the guy holding a little statue right now.

cards.question: What happens to everyone who worships images and boasts in idols?

cards.text: Then the singer calls out to the gods themselves: "Worship Him, all you gods!" Everybody to the floor, friend, no matter how big your title is.
Now notice the switch: the singer stops talking about the LORD and starts talking to Him. Meanwhile, Zion is listening, and so are the towns of Judah.

cards.question: Zion and the towns of Judah tremble in fear because of the LORD's judgments.
The singer tells the LORD why Zion is glad. Compared to all gods, where does the LORD stand?

cards.text: Then the singer turns to everyone who loves the LORD with a command. Short. Simple. ZERO wiggle room.

cards.question: ___ evil, O you who love the LORD!
For those who love Him, the psalm says the LORD preserves the souls of His saints.

cards.text: And He delivers them from the hand of the wicked. Friend, I know a little something about getting pulled out of a dark place, and let me tell you, it NEVER gets old.

cards.question: The singer has a promise for God's people: Light shines on the ___, gladness on the upright in heart.

cards.text: One last line, friend, and it's for the righteous ones. I always save the best topping for last, so let's see if this singer does too.

cards.question: How does the psalm end? What does it tell the righteous ones to do?

answers.text: Rejoice and praise His holy name
Keep quiet and wait for Him
Build Him a house of cedar

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'sleeps' and 'laughs' are silly reactions to lightning lighting up the world, so 'trembles' stands out without any reasoning.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The setup joke ('With fire and lightning everywhere, I would NOT want to be the guy holding a little statue right now') signals a bad outcome for idol worshipers. That rules out card 2's wrong answers 'They are left alone' and 'They are made rich' before the baker answers. It also links the fire of v3 to the idol worshipers, a link the text leaves open.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Zion is listening, and so are the towns of Judah' says the towns of Judah are listening. Psalm 97:8 says only that Zion hears. The towns of Judah exult.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences ('Then the singer turns... with a command.' 'Short.' 'Simple.' 'ZERO wiggle room.'). It is not the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question calls Psalm 97:11 'a promise for God's people.' The text states it ('Light shines on the righteous') and doesn't call it a promise. Saying 'God's people' also hints against the wrong answer 'nations'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
